# Dylan McDermott

> Meteorologist and geospatial data professional building Python pipelines, research tools, and reliable environmental data systems across agriculture and weather.

## Profile

- Location: West Des Moines, Iowa, USA
- Current role: Meteorologist, Property & Liability Resource Bureau (January 2025-Present)
- Education: M.S. and B.S. in Meteorology, Iowa State University
- Contact: dylanddermott@gmail.com
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/dylan-mcdermott-193b18174/

## Work Examples

- [PLRB - Meteorologist](https://dylanmcd16.github.io/work/plrb-weather-systems/): Builds weather-data pipelines and claims-facing ArcGIS applications with validated catastrophe data.
- [Corteva - Research Associate](https://dylanmcd16.github.io/work/corteva-field-sensing/): Co-developed field-sensing systems and independently built Python and ArcPy workflows for GPS-linked measurements at seven research sites, producing plot-level summaries and saving roughly 100 hours across the campaign.
- [Master's Thesis - Iowa State University](https://dylanmcd16.github.io/work/land-use-convective-weather/): Ran WRF with Noah-MP at 50 km to compare present-day and 1850 vegetation during the 1993 and 2008 Midwest flood periods, analyzing simulated rainfall, surface fluxes, and moisture transport.
- [Iowa Severe Weather Explorer](https://dylanmcd16.github.io/projects/iowa-severe-weather-explorer/): Built an interactive replay of the August 10, 2020 Iowa derecho, combining NEXRAD, surface observations, HRRR, GOES-16, warnings, storm reports, and damage data on one timeline.
- [Iowa Soybean Season Explorer](https://dylanmcd16.github.io/projects/iowa-soybean-season-explorer/): A descriptive 2025 season timelapse across 248 central Iowa fields, combining 59 usable Sentinel-2 dates and MRMS radar rainfall.

## Awards

- Esri Special Achievement in GIS (SAG) Award, 2025 - contributed to the PLRB catastrophe analytics and ArcGIS applications recognized by the award.
- AWS 10,000 AIdeas Competition Semi-Finalist - AI Weather Intelligence Platform (independently developed AI weather intelligence platform that extracts evidence from scattered environmental data and generates responses, reports, maps, plots, and more).

## Core Capabilities

- Meteorology & Weather Analysis: Analyze radar, satellite, and model data for severe-weather verification and claims investigations. Evaluate datasets for bias, resolution, provenance, and appropriate interpretation. Tools and methods: NEXRAD / MRMS, GOES, ERA5, Observations & model guidance.
- Numerical Modeling & Scientific Computing: Design WRF and Noah-MP experiments, translate CESM/LUMIP land-use inputs to model grids, and analyze rainfall, surface fluxes, and moisture transport. Tools and methods: WRF / Noah-MP, CESM / LUMIP, Python, MATLAB / NetCDF.
- Python Pipelines & Data Stewardship: Apply FAIR-aligned stewardship: document sources and fields, manage access, and acquire, standardize, and validate environmental data. Reconcile late reports and detect duplicates, missing timestamps, invalid identifiers, and failed downloads in daily production workflows. Tools and methods: Python, ArcPy, REST APIs, AWS / Linux.
- Geospatial Processing & Web GIS: Build spatial workflows with GPS filtering, inward plot buffers, spatial joins, and raster/vector processing. Develop claims-facing maps with custom filters and synchronized layers. Tools and methods: ArcGIS Pro & Enterprise, ArcPy, Experience Builder, Spatial ETL.
- Field Instrumentation & Agricultural Research: Co-develop GPS-linked sensing platforms, automated soil-gas systems, and reference weather stations. Compare canopy measurements with drone imagery, LiDAR, and crop-stress response. Tools and methods: Trimble GPS, IRT and PAR sensors, Drone imagery / LiDAR, Sensor calibration.
- Applied AI & Scientific Tooling: Build scientific agents with LLM orchestration, multi-step tool calling, structured outputs, and provenance controls. Implement agent evaluation with regression tests, scientific replay, and evidence-grounded answer review. Tools and methods: OpenAI API, Python / FastAPI, React, Supabase.

## Independent AI Development

Independently developed outside work using Python, FastAPI, React, and the OpenAI Responses API. LLM orchestration connects multi-step tool calls and schema-constrained answers with observations, radar, satellite, model, and weather-event data. Scientific tools transform tabular, gridded, and geospatial datasets through derived variables, statistical summaries, and spatial and temporal analysis. Agent evaluation uses regression tests, scientific replay, and answer review against retained evidence. Plotting and multi-address scaling remain under development.

## Smartstick Research

Co-developed Smartstick with IRT and PAR sensors for research across seven sites. Built a Python and ArcPy processing proof of concept in approximately one week, reducing processing from about one hour to five minutes per collection. I led coordination with teams in California, Puerto Rico, Texas, and Chile, reviewing sensor setups and measurement data and guiding changes to standardize collection methods across sites. I trained teammates and refined the code from their feedback. The team continued using the pipeline to process and analyze data after I left.
